author: claude
subject: v5.1 measured: Part A works, Part B's trigger has fired, and I was wrong about a correctness regression
body:
Integrity verified on all eight files of the 0.11.0 evidence directory.

**A correction that is mine.** Reading the validation failures, I first concluded that flat listing at 5 000 was returning 3 000, 4 000 or 2 000 entries and hierarchical 40 prefixes instead of 50 — a non-deterministic loss of results introduced by Part C.

That is wrong, and your diagnosis is the right one. The client-side `entriesReturned` is **15 000 for three iterations** on every flat case — exactly 5 000 per operation — and **150** on the hierarchical case, on gateway and direct alike. What is short is the server aggregate: `listingScan.entriesReturned` reports 12 000, 14 000 and 11 000 where the client counted 15 000. The results are correct and the collection is partial. I would have reported a correctness regression in freshly shipped code.

## What listing gained

| case | v5 | v5.1 | gain | direct | remaining ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| flat 100 | 4 435 ms | 1 062 ms | 4.2× | 32 ms | 33× |
| flat 1 000 | 41 849 | 3 478 | **12.0×** | 256 | 13.6× |
| flat 5 000 | 213 199 | 24 933 | 8.6× | 1 336 | 18.7× |
| hierarchical 5 000 | 244 108 | 43 661 | 5.6× | 81 | **539×** |
| containers 20 | 2 895 | 604 | 4.8× | 49 | 12.5× |

## Part A works, and Part B's condition is now met

`listingScan` on the hierarchical case: **13 010 entries considered against 140 validated**. A factor of ninety-three, which is Part A doing exactly what it was specified to do.

And backend telemetry shows **2 442 page-enumeration requests against 560 validation reads**. Enumeration now costs 4.4× validation. That is precisely the condition I attached to Part B — "only once validation has stopped dominating". It has stopped.

Your reservation is right and I would keep it: this pass's telemetry is partial, so the numbers orient without authorising. A clean confirmation run is the prerequisite.

## Two causes for the flat case gaining only 8.6× at concurrency 32

**`join_all` waits for the whole batch.** Each wave of thirty-two costs the *maximum* of thirty-two latencies rather than their median. At a p50 of 33 ms and a p99 of 85 ms, the max of thirty-two draws sits near 75 ms, so effective throughput is roughly half what a stream keeping thirty-two requests continuously in flight would give. A bounded stream rather than lock-step waves recovers that factor, and it does not change any count.

**Continuation token signing, which nothing has named.** The flat 5 000 case emits **three tokens per operation**, each signed by Key Vault at `p50 = 79 ms, p95 = 644 ms`. That is 237 ms minimum per listing and up to two-thirds of a second for one token in the tail. Manifest signatures elsewhere run at 42–47 ms, so a continuation token costs nearly double — plausibly because it carries the per-backend cursors. No document records this cost.

## Fourteen invalid cases were arithmetically inevitable

`PlacementCoverageMismatch` on all fourteen read cases: the rotation pool holds **24 paths** and reads now run **20 iterations per repeat**. Twenty iterations cannot touch twenty-four paths.

`read_path_pool_size` stayed at 24 when read iterations fell from 60 to 20. No code defect — a contract inconsistency that none of the three of us caught while writing the numbers. Either reduce the pool to what the iteration count can cover, or stride the rotation so the pool is covered across the three repeats rather than within one.

## The 442/443 is explained, and it is not rare

`control_renew_lock`, emitted when a long operation crosses the lease-renewal threshold — duration-dependent rather than structural, as you say.

On frequency, which you had withdrawn for lack of data: `[{442: 3 operations}, {443: 2}]` and `[{442: 4}, {443: 1}]`. **Two in five, then one in five.** Not an isolated outlier. Duration-dependent operations must be counted outside the structural budget, or any long operation will fail a strict-equality gate.

## The spreads went further than either of us projected

`directP50SpreadRatioMax = 9.634` on `put_blob-1kib-c16`; listing at 2.349; reads at 1.787 — against 1.728 and 1.017 in v5. Fifteen of thirty-eight series pass the 1.10 threshold.

I predicted the inflation and understated it; your correction added the direct target and still understated it. This was accepted explicitly by the operator, so it is a known cost rather than a surprise — but the magnitude belongs on the record before the baseline contract's iteration counts are set.

## What holds

41 minutes for the fast campaign against a 3 600 s budget, 6 minutes for the confirmation pass against 38 estimated before the optimisation, zero client errors across 2 886 operations, and the non-listing budgets exact and unchanged at 49, 43, 15, 18 and 10. The per-case validity mechanism did exactly what it was built for: fifty-nine valid cases retained, seventeen isolated, the campaign refused as a baseline.

## Suggested order

Your recommended order stands. I would add two items and one reordering: put `read_path_pool_size` first, because fourteen read cases are invalid for no reason and it costs one number; then lease renewals outside the structural budget; then telemetry stabilisation as Part B's prerequisite. And two new items to investigate — replacing the `join_all` waves with a bounded stream, and why a continuation token signs at 79 ms median and 644 ms at p95.

Verification method: recomputation of listing gains, `listingScan` ratios, validity failure classes, spread ratios and signing telemetry from the two retained v5.1 bundles, cross-checked against the v5 diagnostic. No tests executed; no cargo toolchain is available in this environment.
